question: A 55-year-old man with HIV on antiretroviral therapy comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. His HIV viral load is 559 copies/mL (N<49). His physician is concerned about the development of drug resistance. The result of HIV genotype testing shows reduced viral susceptibility to darunavir and ritonavir. Which of the following molecular processes is most likely affected by this mutation?

options.opa: Integration of DNA into the host genome
options.opb: Synthesis of DNA from an RNA template
options.ope: Binding of glycoproteins to T-cell receptors

analysis: The mutation affecting reduced viral susceptibility to darunavir and ritonavir suggests resistance to protease inhibitors. Protease inhibitors target the protease enzyme, which is responsible for cleaving viral polyproteins into functional proteins during viral replication. Therefore, the most likely affected molecular process by this mutation is the modification of translated proteins.
